note: Corpus cases where SEAM is knowingly allowed to differ from the legacy engine, each with a reason. The list is a ratchet in both directions: an unlisted difference fails, and a listed case that starts matching fails too. Most differences are now SEAM wins - flows SEAM finds that legacy cannot, because its summaries iterate to a fixpoint over the SCC condensation, because it carries taint through package-level globals, or because its model database covers cgo and template-injection sinks legacy has no rule family for.

cases.bufio-scanner/all: SEAM materialises one bufio finding inside the stdlib under --dataflow all; legacy, which has no summary for (*bufio.Scanner).Text, reports none. The finding is real - the scanner's Text() returns attacker-controlled data - but the standard library is out of scope for the default report.
cases.cgo-string-roundtrip/security: SEAM recognises every cgo wrapper via the _Cfunc_ prefix sink and models the conversion functions, so it reports four slices (one per boundary call plus the command-execution flow); legacy reports three (it has no source for C.GoString and so collapses the duplicate). The shape SEAM reports is correct, just stricter.
cases.context-value/security: SEAM reports the command-execution flow twice and legacy once. The two slices have different sources for the same data: r.FormValue("cmd") and the *http.Request parameter itself, which SEAM sees through the type-shaped source model and legacy's pattern pack does not reach here. Both routes are real, so neither is dropped; enrichment marks the second with duplicateOf/flowKey, which is the mechanism for collapsing them at presentation time.
cases.deep-chain-8-levels/security: SEAM finds it and legacy does not: SEAM iterates summaries to a fixpoint over the SCC condensation, legacy iterates a fixed four times (defect 11).
cases.defer-taint/security: SEAM finds it and legacy does not: SEAM maps a closure's FreeVar indices back to the caller's MakeClosure bindings (so a deferred closure that sinks a captured value is detected), legacy has no equivalent closure-summary application.
cases.dep-drops-taint-negative/all: Under --dataflow all SEAM materialises the dependency and finds the real HelperFromRequest->RunCommand flow. Legacy also finds a flow but for the wrong reason: its blanket propagation rule assumes Drop returns its argument (defect 16), when Drop actually returns a constant. Both engines report the same source->sink category pair; the fixture sanctions the flow with a want annotation rather than testing which internal path was taken.
cases.dep-only-flow/all: The flow lies entirely inside a dependency. SEAM summarises reachable dependency functions and now reports the flow from the local caller through the dependency's summary (defect 8 closed: source models no longer fire during summary computation, so param-to-sink summaries are recorded correctly).
cases.dep-only-flow/security: SEAM finds it and legacy does not: the callee's summary now records the param-to-sink flow (defect 8), and the slice materialises under the local caller's context. Legacy has no summary for the dependency function.
cases.dep-transitive-2-hops/all: SEAM reports the flow once where legacy reports it twice, emitting a second slice through the dependency's internal path.
cases.func-field-dispatch/security: SEAM resolves a call through a func-typed struct field by indexing every function stored into that field program-wide (funcfield.go); legacy has no equivalent and stops at the field read, so the expectation is marked known-fail=legacy:32.
cases.func-param-callback/security: SEAM finds both flows and legacy neither: a call through a function-valued parameter, which nothing static can name, propagates its argument taint to its result (defect 33 closed for SEAM).
cases.generic-constraint-method/security: SEAM finds it and legacy does not: a call on a type-parameter-typed value is an unresolvable invoke in the generic origin and a static call in the instantiation, and SEAM prefers the instantiation summary (defect 22 closed for SEAM).
cases.generic-container/security: SEAM finds the flow through a generic container and legacy does not: SEAM keys summaries on fn.Origin() so an instantiation's summary is the origin's, while legacy's per-instantiation keying never finds it (defect 22).
cases.generic-method/security: SEAM finds both flows and legacy neither. Two SEAM capabilities combine: field-qualified taint survives the by-value copies a value-typed composite literal and a value receiver compile to, and a call through a function-valued parameter propagates its argument taint to its result. Legacy has neither, so the expectations are marked known-fail=legacy:33.
cases.global-var-carrier/security: SEAM finds it and legacy does not: SEAM has a program-wide global taint map, legacy carries no taint through package-level variables (defect 19).
cases.interface-dispatch/security: SEAM resolves interface dispatch through its implements-index (defect 3 closed); legacy cannot, so the expectation is marked known-fail=legacy:3.
cases.linkname/security: SEAM finds it and legacy does not: SEAM follows a //go:linkname directive from the body-less declaration to the implementing function, using the mapping the call graph already draws its alias edge from (defect 25 closed for SEAM).
cases.promoted-field-literal-key/security: SEAM finds the flow and legacy does not: taint entering a struct through a promoted key in a composite literal survives the whole-aggregate load and store the value-typed literal compiles to (defect 34 closed for SEAM).
cases.slice-of-pointer/security: SEAM finds it and legacy does not: SEAM marks the base allocation tainted when a field is stored, so a returned pointer carries field taint (defect 21).
cases.template-injection/security: SEAM finds it and legacy does not: SEAM has html/template sink models, legacy has no template rule family (defect 24).
cases.value-receiver-field/security: SEAM finds the flow and legacy does not: the receiver spill a value receiver compiles to (*t0 = c) widens whole-value taint to the aggregate's field view, so a method can see taint in its own receiver's fields (defect 34 closed for SEAM).
cases.worker-pool/security: SEAM finds it and legacy does not: SEAM applies a closure's summary at the launch site using the converged block-output state (so a goroutine that receives from a channel sent to later in the same caller is detected), legacy has no equivalent asynchronous summary application (defect 7).
